children.text: A waterfall about 98m high in the Campangga valley of Barili on Cebu's west coast, considered the tallest on the island. The 14m falls near the entrance, the hanging bridge, bamboo rafting in front of the main falls, and swimming are all in one place, which makes it a good day trip from Cebu City.
Mantayupan Falls is in Barangay Campangga, in the town of Barili, about
southwest of Cebu City. In a valley that runs inland from the Tañon Strait on Cebu's west coast, the falls come in two tiers. The main falls at the back is about
high and is presented as the tallest waterfall in Cebu province. Near the entrance, a smaller falls about

high and a round pool appear first. Locals also call it Ambakan, from a Cebuano word meaning "to jump," and both names sit side by side on the big signboard at the entrance. Note that Wikipedia gives the height as about

Before it was a tourist spot, this was the village's water source. The valley's water irrigates the rice paddies and fish ponds downstream, and a small hydropower plant run on the falls' water was reported by a local newspaper in

to send about 1MW to the Cebu electric cooperative. Admission and facilities are understood to be run by a village cooperative (CAMPCO). Barili is an agricultural town of 42 barangays, with a parish founded in
, and it still has an old church and wooden mansions.
the falls once dried up for a while. In

a sinkhole about 60cm wide and about 3.7m deep opened in the upstream riverbed, the river drained underground, and the falls, rice paddies, fish ponds, and power plant all lost their water. The Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB-7) pointed to the possibility of an underground cave beneath the river, and the village dug a bypass channel of about

and plugged the hole with sandbags to bring the water back. The blow was severe: weekends that normally drew 500 visitors saw only 50 by noon. Today it is crowded with local families again every weekend.

Its biggest strength is accessibility. Step down from the parking area toward the entrance signboard and picnic tables and you can look up at the falls; walk past the pool of the first falls and cross the hanging bridge, and in about
you reach the emerald pool in front of the main falls. It needs no long trek or canyoning as Kawasan Falls does, so children and older visitors can go too, and since it is
from Cebu City by bus, a day trip is possible.
It is easy to visit as a day trip from Cebu City, and it also fits as one stop on a southwest Cebu loop combined with the sardine-run snorkeling at

. It is recommended for families and groups of friends who would rather lay out a packed lunch and splash in the valley than visit a crowded tourist spot, and for photo-minded travelers. Be prepared for weekend-afternoon crowds and small fees collected at various points.
Cross the hanging bridge and go deeper into the valley, and a single ribbon of water about

long drops between mossy green cliffs, with a deep turquoise pool below. In the dry season the stream falls thin and long; in the rainy season it falls thick and muddy. The cliffs are shaded in the morning, so photos come out more even than in strong midday sun.

blocks.title: The 14m falls and first pool at the entrance

children.text: Just below the entrance, the first falls, about

high, splits into several streams and drops into a round pool. It is deep enough to swim in and can be seen from the picnic tables in front of the entrance signboard, which makes it easy to keep an eye on children.

blocks.title: The hanging bridge across the valley

children.text: Cross the narrow hanging bridge over the valley between the first falls and the main falls, and the main falls is about
away. After the bridge you must walk a short, rocky path, and since the bridge sways, keep the number of people crossing at once low.

blocks.title: Bamboo raft in front of the main falls

children.text: At the pool of the main falls you can ride a bamboo raft that is pulled by a rope or paddled up to the falls, and getting pounded by the water, like a waterfall massage, is the signature experience here. Fares differ by source:
notice, so budget a range of about
. You ride in a life vest and should expect to get soaked.

blocks.title: Swimming in the pool and rock jumping

children.text: The main falls pool is deep, so wearing a life vest (about
) is a must if you swim. On the right side of the pool there is a ledge about

high, reached by stepping on footholds in the rock, and some people jump from it. On murky days you cannot see the rocks and trash on the bottom, and one review even says the writer did not jump, so do not push yourself.
There are huts, tables and chairs, and charcoal grill rental spaces at the entrance and across the bridge, which makes it a good place to stay for half a day. Huts start at about
, and one review says tables and chairs are charged separately, so ask first.

is the rainy season, with monthly rainfall of about 186–191mm and 27–28 rainy days. The falls are at their most magnificent, but muddy water often comes down, and swimming is sometimes closed for safety after heavy rain. In some years Cebu is hit by typhoons between
Typhoon Kalmaegi (local name Tino) caused severe flooding across Cebu island. The valley's water can rise suddenly, so check the forecast.

Mantayupan Falls is a day trip from Cebu City, so most people stay in Cebu City or Mactan. Overnight huts at the falls are advertised from about
, but the facilities are basic, so inquire in advance. If you are touring southwest Cebu over several days, it is more convenient to stay at Panagsama Beach in
away by car. Guesthouses run about

At the falls entrance and across the bridge there are stalls selling grilled meat, rice, and drinks, but the choices are limited and prices are on the high side. Like local families, many people buy roast chicken, puso (rice wrapped in palm leaves), and tropical fruit at Barili market, but ask at the entrance whether outside food is charged a bring-in fee. On the way into town there is a milk station selling goat's milk and milk, which is worth a snack stop. If you stop in
on the way back, you can try crispy fried pork rind chicharon and market lechon, and in Cebu City the Cebu-style whole roast pig lechon is a must.
Admission, the raft, and habal-habal are mostly cash. One review says to bring about
if you also want chairs, a table, and food, and there is no ATM near the falls.
. They may change with the weather and events, so check the notice on the official page before visiting.
It is crowded all day on weekends, so going on a weekday morning gives you quieter surroundings and better photos.
Rocks and wet paths are slippery, so wear aqua shoes or strap sandals, and avoid going barefoot given the rocky path across the bridge.
Bring a dry bag, a change of clothes, and a towel, and you can head back comfortably even after riding the raft and getting hit by the falls.
Because GPS is weak inside the valley, launch a drone from the parking lot and fly it toward the falls.
Return buses thin out around sunset, so be back in Barili town before
After heavy rain, the valley's water can rise suddenly and muddy water can come down, so if the caretaker stops swimming you must comply. In
, at Tinubdan Falls in Catmon, northern Cebu, three swimmers died when a torrent surged suddenly after only light rain.
The middle of the main falls pool is deep. If you are not confident in the water, be sure to wear a life vest, and a guardian should watch children from close by.

Keep the number of people on the hanging bridge low, and do not run or shake it.
Mosquitoes are common in the valley, so bring insect repellent, and walk slowly so you do not slip on wet rocks.
The falls' water is used for rice paddies, fish ponds, power generation, and the village's own needs, so do not use soap or shampoo or throw away trash.
